findings.body:
`skipped` still says “skipped by the label gate” after this PR extended the output to cover the `skip-review-label` emergency bypass as well.

`action.yml` and `README.md` already describe both paths; the setup skill is the local companion manual (AGENTS.md Rule #7 / extension “action.yml change must be mirrored in setup/reference.md”). Agents answering “when is `skipped` true?” will miss the bypass path.

```suggestion
| `skipped` | Whether the run was skipped without invoking the LLM (`true`/`false`). Set when the label/author gate suppressed the run **or** the configured `skip-review-label` emergency bypass fired. |
```

This NO-OP case is stale after the three-signal OR for `reviewed_label_applied`.

If a **prior successful** run already armed the bit and stamped the label, a later **blocked** follow-up does **not** clear it: `compute_reviewed_label_applied` keeps `prior_bit` / `label_currently_on_pr`. Condition (c) still holds, so removing the reviewed label after a blocked follow-up **does** fire `USER_FORCED_RESET`.

As written, a maintainer running the smoke test after a blocked re-review will misdiagnose a real reset as a regression. Narrow the NO-OP to “previous run never successfully armed the bit (e.g. first-ever review was blocked, or no prior successful stamp)” — matching `docs/ITERATION_AWARENESS.md` § 8.5.

The empty-`bot_login` fallback is documented here (and in the matching test) as “over-review, never under-surface.” That is incorrect for IAR marker fetch.

With `bot_login=""`, `_fetch_latest_marker_body` accepts **any** author. Under default `collapse-previous: true`, a non-bot comment carrying `REVIEW_MARKER` + a forged `open_fingerprints_this_gen` list can win tier 1 and **silence non-critical findings** — under-surface, not over-review. Criticals still pass the § 7.1 rail; warnings/infos do not.

`gh_get_authenticated_login` almost always returns a login (tier-4 default), so this path is rare — but the comment trains the wrong failure mode. Prefer: “filter off → pre-round-10 forgery window for non-criticals; prefer failing closed or defaulting `bot_login` to `DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_BOT_LOGIN` instead of `""`.”

`scripts/reviewer.py` is now ~6836 LOC after the IAR landing — well past the ~4500 soft ceiling in `docs/STANDARDS.md` § File size.

Not a merge blocker (extension de-escalates this to info; the split is a scheduled decision). Worth tracking as its own PR so the single-file stdlib runtime invariant can be reviewed deliberately rather than growing another 3k LOC on the next feature.

## Verdict

Solid, high-stakes IAR + skip-review landing. Runtime invariants (critical-always-surfaces, five-condition `USER_FORCED_RESET`, three-tier marker fetch, label-stamp-before-embed, try/except fallback, skip short-circuit before side effects, collision guard) look correct and are locked by a large unit suite. Remaining issues are operator-facing drift and one mislabeled security fallback — nothing that should block merge if you treat the warnings as polish before tag.

## What I verified

- **Public contract:** 4 IAR inputs + 5 outputs + `skip-review-label` wired through `action.yml` → env → `main()`; no removals of existing inputs/outputs.
- **Safety rails:** `dedupe_findings_against_prior` critical branch; `_sort_findings_criticals_first` before both truncation sites; `label_stamped` observed before state embed; `label_fetch_ok` on reset; escape skipped on `USER_FORCED_RESET`; three-dot range hash / safety-net denominator.
- **Security surfaces:** stdlib-only imports; argv-list `subprocess`; `safe_repo_path` on `git show`; hardcoded `IAR_EXHAUSTIVE_PROMPT_ADDENDUM`; marker author + provider filters; parser coercion for fingerprints / history / `reviewed_label_applied`; skip path does not stamp `applied-label` or touch IAR state.
- **Docs/examples:** `examples/skip-review-label.yml` and `iteration-aware.yml` use `env`-safe patterns and explicit `permissions:`; self-review dogfoods IAR + skip.
